subject.title: Slack: Include file attachment metadata in inbound message delivery to agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared cross-channel inbound attachment metadata contract for agents, or keep Slack file details limited to the existing placeholder, MediaPath/MediaTypes, and download-file surfaces?
rationale: The missing metadata is real, but the durable fix changes the agent-facing channel/plugin context API rather than only Slack internals.

options.title: Add shared attachment metadata
options.body: Introduce a channel-agnostic attachment metadata block and populate Slack file id, name, MIME type, and size without replacing existing media fields.

options.title: Keep current file access surfaces
options.body: Continue relying on placeholders, MediaPath/MediaTypes, and download-file, and close or defer the request as outside the current agent context contract.

options.title: Add a Slack-only field
options.body: Expose Slack-specific metadata now, accepting future cleanup risk if other transports need the same contract.

recommendation.title: Add shared attachment metadata
recommendation.body: Introduce a channel-agnostic attachment metadata block and populate Slack file id, name, MIME type, and size without replacing existing media fields.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across Slack media handling and shared channel context seams.
